## Household and background

Cameron Monroe (born January 30, 1976) is single with no dependents and lives at 22 Alder Court in Anytown. Cameron dispatches trucks at Ridgeline Freight Services — one W-2, box 1 wages $58,640.00, box 2 federal withholding $5,310.00.

In May, a $10.00 state-lottery scratch ticket paid a prize of $8,160.00. The PROCEEDS — the $8,160.00 prize minus the $10.00 wager = $8,150.00 — are over the $5,000 lottery threshold, so the commission withheld the mandatory 24% of the proceeds, exactly $1,956.00, and issued a Form W-2G (box 1 $8,160.00; box 3 type of wager: state lottery, $10.00 ticket; box 4 $1,956.00). Cameron also kept buying tickets the rest of the year — about $1,240.00 of losing tickets, receipts in a shoebox.

## Interview

**Q.** Any gambling winnings besides the one W-2G — smaller prizes, casino play?

**A.** A few $20 scratch wins I put straight back into tickets; nothing else reportable and no casino trips.

**Q.** Can I deduct the $1,240 of losing tickets?

**A.** My preparer says no on this return: gambling losses are an itemized deduction, up to winnings, and my itemizable expenses are nowhere near the standard deduction — so the winnings are reported in full and the losses don't reduce them.

**Q.** Any dependents? Could anyone claim you as a dependent? Are you blind, disabled, or a student? A U.S. citizen all year?

**A.** No to all of those, and yes — citizen all year.

## Preparer notes

- W-2G: lottery PROCEEDS (winnings minus the wager: $8,160 − $10 = $8,150) over $5,000 → mandatory 24% regular gambling withholding on the proceeds ($8,150 × 24% = $1,956.00, box 4) — unlike slot-machine winnings, where regular withholding would not apply. Line 8b still carries the box-1 winnings ($8,160) — the proceeds rule sets only the withholding base.
- Losses ($1,240) are stated, not netted: deductible only as a Schedule A itemized deduction up to winnings; this return takes the $15,750 standard deduction, so line 8b carries the winnings gross.
- Total income $66,800; taxable income $51,050; tax $6,151; withholding $5,310 + $1,956 = $7,266 → a refund.
